arxiv-2106-02529.title: Blockchain for Transactive Energy Management of Distributed Energy Resources in Smart Grid Conference: The Twelfth ACM International Conference on Future Energy Systems; June 28–July 2, 2021; Virtual Event, Italy The Twelfth ACM International Conference on Future Energy Systems (e-Energy ’21), June
arxiv-2106-02529.creator: Qing Yang, Hao Wang, Xiaoxiao Wu, Taotao Wang, Shengli Zhang
arxiv-2106-02529.description: Abstract . This work presents the design and implementation of a blockchain system that enables the trustable transactive energy management for distributed energy resources (DERs). We model the interactions among DERs, including energy trading and flexible appliance scheduling, as a cost minimization problem.

arxiv-2111-02983.title: Turing patterns with space varying diffusion coefficients: eigenfunctions satisfying the Legendre equation
arxiv-2111-02983.creator: Elkinn A. Calderón-Barreto, José L. Aragón
arxiv-2111-02983.description: Abstract The problem of pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems with space varying diffusion is studied. On this regard, it has already been shown that the necessary conditions for Turing instability are the same as for the case of homogeneous diffusion, but the sufficient conditions depend on the specific space dependence of the diffusion coefficient.

arxiv-2308-07328.title: Bifurcating periodic solution from a blood flow with variable body force: via Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem This paper was jointly supported from Natural Science Foundation of Zhejiang Province (No. LZ23A010001), National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 11671176, 11931016).
arxiv-2308-07328.creator: Yuchao He Yongli Song Yonghui Xia
arxiv-2308-07328.description: Abstract This paper employs the Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem to investigate the existence of periodic solutions in blood flow propagating through vessels with free boundary conditions. It is rigorously proved that a local C 1 C^{1} -curve of small-amplitude periodic solutions is bifurcated.

arxiv-2409-01922.creator: Ján Mináč, Tung T. Nguyen, Nguy ê ~ \tilde{\text{\^{e}}} n Duy Tân
arxiv-2409-01922.description: Abstract . Due to their elegant and simple nature, unitary Cayley graphs have been an active research topic in the literature. These graphs are naturally connected to several branches of mathematics, including number theory, finite algebra, representation theory, and graph theory. In this article, we study the perfectness property of these graphs.

arxiv-2505-22322.title: A Closer Look on Memorization in Tabular Diffusion Model: A Data-Centric Perspective
arxiv-2505-22322.creator: Zhengyu Fang zxf177@case.edu, Zhimeng Jiang zhimengj@tamu.edu, Huiyuan Chen hxc501@case.edu, Xiaoge Zhang xxz705@case.edu, Kaiyu Tang kxt439@case.edu, Xiao Li xxl1015@case.edu, Jing Li jingli@cwru.edu
arxiv-2505-22322.description: Abstract Diffusion models have shown strong performance in generating high-quality tabular data, but they carry privacy risks by inadvertently reproducing exact training samples. While prior work focuses on data augmentation for memorization mitigation, little is known about which individual samples contribute the most to memorization.

arxiv-2509-26115.title: Tracer diffusion coefficients in a sheared granular gas. Exact results
arxiv-2509-26115.creator: David González Méndez, Vicente Garzó
arxiv-2509-26115.description: Abstract The diffusion of tracer particles immersed in a granular gas under uniform shear flow (USF) is analyzed within the framework of the inelastic Boltzmann equation. Two different but complementary approaches are followed to achieve exact results. First, we maintain the structure of the Boltzmann collision operator but consider inelastic Maxwell models (IMM).

arxiv-2510-26575.title: InfoFlow: Reinforcing Search Agent Via Reward Density Optimization
arxiv-2510-26575.creator: Kun Luo 1,2 Hongjin Qian 1 Zheng Liu 1 Ziyi Xia 1 Shitao Xiao 1 Siqi Bao 3 Jun Zhao 2 Kang Liu 2 1 Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence 2 Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences 3 Baidu Inc. {luokun695, chienqhj, ziyixia85, zhengliu1026}@gmail.com kliu@nlpr.ia.ac.cn
arxiv-2510-26575.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a promising approach for enhancing agentic deep search. However, its application is often hindered by low Reward Density in deep search scenarios, where agents expend significant exploratory costs for infrequent and often null final rewards.

arxiv-2601-12199.title: CTC-DID: CTC-Based Arabic dialect identification for streaming applications
arxiv-2601-12199.creator: Muhammad Umar Farooq, Oscar Saz
arxiv-2601-12199.description: Abstract This paper proposes a Dialect Identification (DID) approach inspired by the Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss function as used in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). CTC-DID frames the dialect identification task as a limited-vocabulary ASR system, where dialect tags are treated as a sequence of labels for a given utterance.

pmc-10608746.title: The Magnetic Technique—A Novel and Promising Method to Improve Axillary Staging Localisation from a Swedish Perspective
pmc-10608746.creator: Fredrik Wärnberg, Christine Obondo, Kian Chin
pmc-10608746.description: The magnetic technique using superparamagnetic nanoparticles of iron oxide has been well established for sentinel lymph node detection. Its main advantage is in the context of logistics, with the possibility to inject several weeks before surgery and the possibility to give access to sentinel lymph node biopsy for women worldwide in places without nuclear medicine facilities.

pmc-11455967.title: Impact of coupled input data source-resolution and aggregation on contributions of high-yielding traits to simulated wheat yield
pmc-11455967.creator: Ehsan Eyshi Rezaei, Babacar Faye, Frank Ewert, Senthold Asseng, Pierre Martre, Heidi Webber
pmc-11455967.description: High-yielding traits can potentially improve yield performance under climate change. However, data for these traits are limited to specific field sites. Despite this limitation, field-scale calibrated crop models for high-yielding traits are being applied over large scales using gridded weather and soil datasets. This study investigates the implications of this practice.

pmc-12570593.title: Brief communication: comprehensive HIV/AIDS knowledge and its associated factors among women of reproductive age in Tanzania
pmc-12570593.creator: Mtoro J Mtoro, Elihuruma Eliufoo Stephano, Sanun Ally Kessy, Jovin R Tibenderana, Victoria Godfrey Majengo, Erick Donard Oguma, Tegemea Patrick Mwalingo, Immaculata P Kessy, Mussa Hassan Bago, Azan Abubakar Nyundo
pmc-12570593.description: Women of reproductive age (WRA) face the greatest burden of the HIV/AIDS epidemic in low- and middle-income countries, including Tanzania. Comprehensive HIV/AIDS knowledge is vital for effective prevention. Using the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey we found that only 15.9% of WRA possessed comprehensive HIV/AIDS knowledge.

pmc-12580789.title: Decoding the Genomic and Functional Landscape of Emerging Subtypes in Ovarian Cancer
pmc-12580789.creator: Giulia Micoli, Kari Lavikka, Yilin Li, Anna Pirttikoski, Daria Afenteva, Wojciech Senkowski, Giovanni Marchi, Anna Vähärautio, Taru A. Muranen, Titta Joutsiniemi, Sakari Hietanen, Anni Virtanen, Krister Wennerberg, Johanna Hynninen, Jaana Oikkonen, Sampsa Hautaniemi
pmc-12580789.description: Five chromosomal instability–based ovarian cancer subtypes display distinct genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical features, with organoid studies revealing subtype-specific therapeutic sensitivities. Introduction Ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC) is the most abundant and aggressive form of ovarian cancer. Molecularly, it is characterized by chromosomal instability (CIN) and high intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity (1–3).

pmc-12615636.title: Rabies virus-vectored Lyme disease vaccine provides long-term protection against tick-transmitted Borrelia burgdorferi
pmc-12615636.creator: Shantel Rios, Bibek Bhattachan, Christoph Wirblich, Anisha Chandwani, Kruthi Vavilikolanu, Jacob F. Myers, Chrysoula Kitsou, Utpal Pal, Matthias J. Schnell
pmc-12615636.description: Lyme disease (LD) cases have doubled globally. LD is a tick-borne illness caused by the Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato (Bb). If untreated, Bb can disseminate to distal organs, causing carditis, arthritis, and meningitis. Currently, no FDA-approved human LD vaccine exists on the market. This study used two approaches to incorporate OspA into the rabies virus (RABV) vaccine vector.

pmc-12669378.title: Trajectories and Predictors of Physical Activity in Women with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in Guangzhou, China: A Prospective Study
pmc-12669378.creator: Hui Zhao, Yutao Lan, Wenxuan Lin, Zhiyun Li
pmc-12669378.description: PurposeThis study analyzed physical activity (PA) trajectories, identified subgroups, and explored their associations in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).MethodsFrom January to November 2024, a longitudinal study was conducted using convenience sampling to recruit women with GDM from a maternal and child health hospital in Guangzhou (China).

pmc-12704185.title: Superiority of TB-PCR Over Conventional and Immunologic Tests for Diagnosing Tuberculosis in Small Bronchoscopic Non-Malignant Specimens
pmc-12704185.creator: Fei Tang, Xiankui Zha, Jieting Zhao, Wei Ye, Liping Lv, Dongchun Ma
pmc-12704185.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn the small non-malignant specimens acquired through respiratory endoscopy, the conventional pathological examination approaches such as acid-fast staining have certain restrictions in the sensitivity of tuberculosis diagnosis.ObjectiveTo investigate the sensitizing effect and clinical value of polymerase chain reaction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (TB-PCR) based on fluorescent probe nucleic acid detection technology in improving the diagnostic positive rate of non-malignant small specimens obtained by respiratory endoscopy.MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 729 patients with suspected TB who underwent respiratory endoscopy.

pmc-12932344.title: Effect of immediate photobiomodulation on pain and inflammation after oral biopsy: A randomized clinical study
pmc-12932344.creator: Yolanda Collado-Murcia, Francisco Parra-Perez, Pia López-Jornet
pmc-12932344.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate whether photobiomodulation (PBM) reduces postoperative pain and inflammation in patients undergoing a soft tissue oral biopsy, compared with a sham treatment.Materials and methodsA prospective, randomized controlled clinical study was conducted. Oral mucosal biopsies were performed using a standardized protocol. Group allocation was carried out using simple randomization.

pmc-12999839.title: Exploring the Influence of Recreational Cannabis Legalization on Women’s Perceptions and Experiences with Perinatal Cannabis Use: A Qualitative Meta-synthesis
pmc-12999839.creator: Kassandra Maturino, Jamie Morton, Karry Weston, Allison Anbari
pmc-12999839.description: ObjectiveWe aimed to explore how women living in places with legalized recreational cannabis perceive perinatal cannabis use, and how legalization potentially impacts their experiences.MethodsBetween September 2024 and December 2025, we searched databases including PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, PsycINFO, and Web of Science. All research reports were screened and evaluated based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

pmc-13146984.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A679 CONTINUATION VERSUS SWITCHING DIRECT ORAL ANTICOAGULANT AFTER BREAKTHROUGH STROKE: A NON-INFERIORITY TARGET TRIAL ANALYSIS FROM THE ASPERA-R STUDY
pmc-13146984.creator: Lucio D'anna, Matteo Foschi, Federico De Santis, Francesca Gabriele, Andrea Zini, Angelo Cascio Rizzo, Leonardo Pantoni, Giovanni Merlino, Barbara Casolla, Blanca Fuentes, Paolo Candelaresi, Diana Aguiar de Sousa, Ahmed Abdelalim, Liqun Zhang, Pietro Caliandro, Giovanni Frisullo, Maria Rosaria Bagna
pmc-13146984.description: Background and aimsManagement strategies after ischemic stroke occurring despite direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) therapy for atrial fibrillation vary widely, and switching anticoagulation is common despite limited supporting evidence. We compared the effectiveness and safety of continuing the same DOAC versus switching to another oral anticoagulant after a breakthrough stroke using a prespecified non-inferiority framework.
